field_notes.name: Sherry vinegar
field_notes.body: Tomatoes are already acidic — sharp vinegar just adds the same note twice. Sherry vinegar is rounder, with a quiet sweetness. It cooperates. Try it anywhere you'd reach for lemon. A mild red wine vinegar works if that's what you have.

field_notes.name: Flaky salt goes on last
field_notes.body: It goes on last — never while cooking. Table salt dissolves in; flaky salt stays on the surface, so you taste it in distinct moments. On a ripe tomato or a peach, that difference is the whole experience. Keep a small dish near where you plate.

field_notes.name: Add herbs after the heat
field_notes.body: The fragrance is gone within seconds of hitting a hot pan. Add basil and mint after the heat is off, or right before the plate reaches the table. The smell will tell you something changed.

field_notes.name: Low heat for rich fish.
field_notes.body: A fatty fish like salmon is at its best cooked gently: a 275°F oven for about twenty minutes, until it just flakes and a few white beads appear at the edges. The fat stays inside, the flesh turns silky, and the window for overcooking is wide. It's the opposite of how most people cook salmon — and the reason it tastes better.

weekend_meal.name: Slow-roasted salmon, tomatoes, and burrata.
weekend_meal.intro: One meal should feel like the reason you went shopping. In July, it's wild salmon cooked so gently it turns silky, next to the best tomatoes of the year — the one cooking lesson this month is built around.
weekend_meal.card_line: Wild salmon, ripe tomatoes, burrata, basil, sourdough
ingredients: 1½ lbs wild salmon, in one piece
weekend_meal.ingredient_note: Everything here is on the shopping list. Wild Pacific salmon — king, sockeye, or coho — is in season through summer. Farmed works with the same timing. What's left is tomorrow's tomato plate.
weekend_meal.method: Heat the oven to 275°F. Set the salmon on an oiled sheet pan, rub it with olive oil, and salt it. Roast for 18 to 25 minutes, depending on thickness, until it flakes when pressed and a few white beads appear at the edges — it will look barely done, and that's right. While it roasts, slice the tomatoes thick, salt them, and set the burrata beside them. Spoon the vinaigrette over the tomatoes, tear basil over everything, and add black pepper. Break the salmon into large pieces at the table. Sourdough for dragging through what's left on the plate.

drink.name: Hillcrest Spritz
drink.intro: One drink. Make it on repeat.
drink.card_line: Tart cherry, mint, lime, sparkling water
drink.method: Fill a rocks glass with ice. Add cherry juice and lime. Slap the mint once between your palms, drop it in, then top with sparkling water. Add more sparkling water to taste.

heirloom-tomatoes.why_now: July is peak tomato season in Southern California. Any ripe tomato — heirloom or not — is at its best right now. The heat concentrates sugars across every variety. Heirlooms are worth it if you see good ones, but a ripe vine tomato from Trader Joe's or Whole Foods will do the same work.
how_to_choose: Heavy for their size
Fragrant at the stem end
Give slightly under gentle pressure

Avoid anything refrigerated at the store

heirloom-tomatoes.price_note: Vine and roma tomatoes are among the most affordable options year-round — and July is when they're actually worth buying. Heirlooms cost more but aren't required.
